main_text.p: netraret, adjutus avaritiâ Genuen-sium mercatorum, qui singulas Turcas pro singulis aureis nummis unâ nocte in Europam navibus suis transportarunt.
main_text.head: Turcæ fracti à Timuro.
main_text.p: (5) Status depressus.Timur, vulgò Tamerlanes, poten-tissimus Tartarorum Imperator cir-ca A.C. 1399. ingenti prælio Bajaze-tham Imperatorem Turcarum supe-ravit, & vivum cavea ferrea inclusit, ac per Asiam spectaculo circumdu-xit.
main_text.head: Potiti Imperio Orientis.
main_text.p: (6) Summum fastigium.Quanquam Turcarum poten-tia dissipata & fracta penitus à Ta-merlane videretur, mox tamen illô discedente Turcæ recollecti Impe-rium amplissimum instaurarunt; ita

page.notes: The catchword "qui" is printed in the lower right corner. The margin labels (5) and (6) are partly cut off at the edge, so "fastigium" is read from the broken syllables "fastigiũ". The word "Turcæ" in the heading is read with some doubt because of the ligature.
